references.text: God confirms His promises to Abraham because he was obedient, which directly connects to the purpose in Genesis 18:19 that the Lord will grant Abraham what He has promised him.
God fulfills His promises to Isaac because Abraham kept His commands, statutes, and laws, confirming Abraham's faithfulness in walking in the Lord's ways.
Moses reminds the people not to forget what they have seen and to teach it to their children and grandchildren, reflecting Abraham's calling to instruct his family in the Lord's ways.
The command to keep God's word on one's heart and impress it upon one's children reflects the same principle as Abraham's commitment to train his family to walk in the Lord's ways.
The exhortation to teach a young person the way he should go reflects Abraham's calling to instruct his children and household in doing what is right and just.
Joshua's declaration that he and his house will serve the Lord reflects the family commitment Abraham was called to, leading his household in the Lord's ways.
Abraham's faith and obedience when he was called show the same attitude that underpinned his commitment to instruct his family in the Lord's ways.
Shows how Abraham's calling to follow the Lord's way (18:19) becomes a reality in the lives of his household and servants (24:48).
Connects Abraham's calling to act righteously (18:19) with the source of his righteousness: faith (Rom 4:3).
Emphasizes that God's promise to Abraham (18:19) stands firm regardless of human self-righteousness (Deut 9:5).
Abraham's calling to do 'right and justice' (18:19) is mirrored in the king's commission to exercise the same righteousness (2 Chron 9:8).
Abraham's calling as 'chosen' to do right (18:19) is a precursor to the Messiah, the chosen servant who brings justice (Isa 42:1).
Connects Abraham's mission to teach his children the Lord's way (18:19) with the definition of the spiritual offspring who live by faith (Rom 4:16).
Genesis 26:5 confirms that Abraham actually lived out the calling to listen and do right as described in 18:19.
Abraham's calling to do 'right and justice' (18:19) finds its messianic fulfillment in the righteous Branch (Jer 33:15).
The promise of the land (Exod 6:8) is inseparably linked to Abraham's call to form a righteous offspring (Gen 18:19).
Abraham's call to do 'right and justice' (Gen 18:19) is reflected in the king's mission (1 Kgs 10:9).
Abraham's call to form a house of obedience (Gen 18:19) is the basis for God's oath to make Israel His people (Deut 29:12).
Abraham's call as 'chosen' (Gen 18:19) is a precursor to the Messiah, the chosen servant (Matt 12:18).
The promise to Isaac (Gen 26:3) confirms that God's plan to fulfill the promise through Abraham's offspring (Gen 18:19) continues.
The principle in Gen 18:19 about 'keeping to the Lord's way' is key to receiving the promises of the land (Deut 30:20).
Abraham's call to do right (Gen 18:19) is a fruit of his righteousness by faith (Gal 3:6).
Abraham's call to do 'right and justice' (Gen 18:19) finds its fulfillment in the righteous Branch (Jer 23:5).
John's mission to turn the hearts of fathers to their children (Luke 1:17) is a restoration of Abraham's call to form a house of obedience (Gen 18:19).
Abraham's righteousness by faith (Gen 15:6) is the basis for his call to do right (Gen 18:19).
The blessing to Jacob (Gen 28:4) continues the promise that is conditioned on obedience (Gen 18:19).
The promise to Jacob (Gen 35:12) continues the promise that is conditioned on obedience (Gen 18:19).
The call to take possession of the land (Deut 1:8) is conditioned on the offspring keeping to the Lord's way (Gen 18:19).
The oaths to Abraham (Luke 1:73) are conditioned on the offspring keeping to the Lord's way (Gen 18:19).
